lens: Cascade integrity, listener ordering doctrine, error isolation per listener, DispatchableAfterCommit semantics, transactional boundary correctness
scope: READ-ONLY analytical pass over the 9 cascade points; structural correctness only; no implementation suggestion past V1.x guardrails
verdict: PASS — structurally sound; one architectural risk noted as RECOMMENDATION-1
executive_summary: The POS → KDS cascade is built on three architectural primitives that interlock cleanly: (1) DispatchableAfterCommit trait that drops events on rollback, (2) the EventServiceProvider declaring listeners in Outbox-FIRST order with a strong inline rationale comment (lines 128-137 + 146-151), and (3) the Outbox-pattern split between PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox (synchronous, SSOT write) and DispatchDomainEventsJob (queued, broadcast). The architectural keystone — 'PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox MUST run first because synchronous queue connections propagate listener exceptions through the dispatcher loop' — is correctly enforced, documented in code, and protected by passing tests (KdsSyncControllerTest, KDSFlowTest, EventContractTest, OutboxConcurrentWorkerDedupeTest — 49 cascade tests green).

findings.analysis: The doctrine 'Outbox-FIRST' is upheld with an explicit comment block (lines 128-137) citing the F-002 round-3 evidence (87 outbox rows pre-id-733, zero post-id-596 when FCM started failing under sync queue). This is a textbook case of architectural intent surviving multiple refactors because the *reason* is in the code, not just a tribal memory.

findings.title: DispatchableAfterCommit guarantees rollback-safety
findings.analysis: Behavior matrix is explicit in the trait header (lines 18-22): outside tx → immediate; inside tx → dispatch after commit; inside tx rollback → dispatch dropped. Order::dispatch() in OrderService::posOrderStore (line 1067) and OrderService::store (line 564) is called *inside* a DB::transaction closure, so the trait engages and prevents the classic 'ghost KDS order on rollback' defect. The pre-existing inline comment '[BUG-C1 FIX] Dispatch notifications AFTER transaction commit — prevents ghost KDS orders on rollback' (OrderService:555) confirms this bug class was historically observed and is now structurally prevented.

findings.title: Outbox row write is atomic and idempotency-keyed BEFORE afterCommit dispatch
findings.analysis: Two-layer idempotency: (1) sha1(event_type|aggregate_id) on a UNIQUE-indexed column (migration 2026_05_09_180000), so concurrent listener firings collapse at the DB level, not just in firstOrCreate logic; (2) wasRecentlyCreated short-circuit so a replay does not re-dispatch the job. The DispatchDomainEventsJob::dispatch is itself wrapped in try/catch (lines 67-78) per the cluster-8 test-e2e fix — a Pusher push failure no longer 500s the HTTP order create.

findings.title: DecrementStockOnOrderCreated re-throws on Throwable — risk of cascade abort if a downstream listener crashes after Outbox write succeeds
findings.analysis: Architecturally, this is *deliberate* (iter12 P1 STOCK 2026-05-09 comment): hard-failing the transaction surfaces orphan rather than silently leaking stock. Since DispatchableAfterCommit fires *after* the surrounding transaction commits, the order row is already durable when this listener runs — a re-throw here will NOT roll back the order, only bubble up to the HTTP response. That means: (a) order is created, (b) outbox row is written (because Outbox runs FIRST), (c) decrement crashes, (d) HTTP 5xx returned to POS cashier. The user-facing UX is: cashier sees error toast, retries, gets idempotency-key 200 OK (existing order). Stock counters DRIFT once by one decrement. This is a *known and accepted* trade-off per the inline rationale, but it should be tracked as a candidate for V1.x: wrap StockUnavailableException only and silently log Throwable, OR add a stock reconciliation job. Status quo is acceptable for V1 single-restaurant.
findings.recommendation: V1.x: introduce a `stock_reconciliation_job` cron that walks orders created in the last hour and reconciles stock_level vs. sum(order_items.qty). Not blocking V1 ship.

findings.title: Three dispatch points for OrderCreated are consistent (all inside transaction commit envelope)
findings.analysis: All four dispatch sites call `\App\Events\OrderCreated::dispatch($order)` inside their respective transaction success branch with the standard try/catch wrapping non-critical Notification dispatches. The trait routes each call through DB::afterCommit. Per-surface cascade is identical: same listener chain, same outbox row, same broadcast channel. Multi-surface consistency — important for V1 single-restaurant where chef KDS is the unifying display — holds.

findings.title: Channel name format is consistent across all 12 Persist*ToOutbox listeners
findings.analysis: Pusher / Laravel-Echo convention: client subscribes via `Echo.private('branch.{id}')` (resources/js/services/eventContract.js:338), server-side broadcast channel name is `private-branch.{id}` (Echo adds the `private-` prefix on the client; broadcaster compares the resolved name in routes/channels.php which declares `branch.{id}`). The 12 listeners and the Echo subscriber match on this contract. EventContract::buildEnvelope and assertEnvelopeValid (last guard before broadcast in DispatchDomainEventsJob:107-110) further enforce the V1 envelope shape, so a malformed payload fails fast as PayloadMismatchException (now fail-once per F-3 SYNC P1 quick-win on lines 174-185).
